newsitem.title: USA: Cargill pays civil penalty in Arab boycott case.
newsitem.headline: Cargill pays civil penalty in Arab boycott case.

text.p: The U.S. Department of Commerce said Friday it imposed a $9,000 civil penalty on Cargill Inc for alleged violations of U.S. measures against the Arab boycott of Israel.

The department had alleged that, during a 1994 export transaction to Syria, Cargill gave Syria information about its business relationships with companies or individuals that were blacklisted under the boycott.
The department also alleged that Cargill knowingly agreed, on two occasions, to refuse to do business with blacklisted companies and individuals.
And, Cargill failed to report boycott-related requests from Syria to U.S. authorities, the department said.

Cargill voluntarily disclosed the alleged violations and cooperated fully during the investigation, the department said. While neither admitting nor denying the allegations, Cargill agreed to pay the civil penalty, the department said.
